newsitem.title: UK: LME slumbers on pre-market, little activity seen.
newsitem.headline: LME slumbers on pre-market, little activity seen.

text.p: Trading in LME metal markets was slow during Friday's pre-market, and after an unexciting stock report and a mini sell-off in lead the complex settled around stable levels.
The movements in LME inventories were fairly small in most cases, ending the first week of daily reporting. Over the week, the big fall has been in copper stocks, down a total of 14,800 tonnes.
Friday's copper stock fall was a light 325 tonnes, however, which left the market basically unmoved. Three months was trading at $2,301 a tonne, down just $1 from Thursday.
In the short term the market needs to hold this level and then clear stubborn upside resistance around $2,310/20. Otherwise, prices may test the $2,280 level, they said.
Lead sagged under $630 at one stage in early business on Far Eastern selling before whipping back again. Recent trade was at $640, up $1 a tonne from yesterday.
Nickel came under pressure from liquidation and some sell-stops, falling to a low of $7,270 before pulling back to $7,303, a $70 decline.
Traders said technical pressures are driving prices lower, with the market ignoring labour problems at New Caledonia.
Aluminium fluctuated aimlessly around Thursday's closing levels, settling at $1,584, down $2. The upside appears to be closed off for the moment, with $1,600 proving to be a stern barrier.
Zinc traded quietly and was unchanged at $1,244. Tin drifted down to $5,660, a $30 loss. Alloy was quoted at $1,460/70 a tonne.
